summary: Post-captive portal: dock interface + IPv6 RA causes WireGuard tunnel route takeover after sleep/resume
description: Issue summary: Multiple engineers on macOS M2 devices using CalDigit TS4 docks report losing access to internal services after their laptops wake from sleep. The zero-trust (WireGuard-based) tunnel shows established, but traffic to internal IPs is routed out the dock/AP link instead of the tunnel. This appears consistently after authenticating to our guest/corporate captive-portal SSID when the dock is connected. Impact: Productivity impact for ~6 engineers across SF office; internal services (git, internal API, vault) unreachable until manual fix or reconnect. Environment: macOS Ventura 13.5 on M2 MacBooks, CalDigit TS4 / Thunderbolt docks, corporate Wi-Fi (802.11ax) with captive portal that performs HTTP redirect authentication, zero-trust agent v1.8.2 and WireGuard kernel tunnel (utun). Observed symptoms: - System shows global IPv6 prefix from AP via SLAAC and a link-local address on dock interface. - Default IPv6 route gets assigned to dock interface with lower metric than utun, client resolves internal hostnames but packets leak to AP, causing connection failures. - Re-establishing zero-trust agent or toggling Wi-Fi fixes temporarily; unplugging dock also fixes. - Repro after sleep/resume is deterministic when dock + captive portal flow are present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect MacBook (Ventura 13.5) to CalDigit TS4 dock into office USB-C port.
2) Join corporate Wi-Fi which redirects to captive portal and complete authentication.
3) Confirm zero-trust agent establishes WireGuard tunnel (utun interface visible).
4) Put MacBook to sleep and wake after ~30s.
5) Attempt to reach internal service (e.g., curl https://internal-api.redwood.local).
6) Observe connection hangs or DNS resolving to internal but TCP/UDP flows fail (packets egress via dock/IPv6 path).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: IPv6 default route from AP/dock is winning over utun route due to interface metric and macOS route selection on dual-stack, causing asymmetric routing and stateful firewall drops inside corporate network.
Confirmed reproduction on two different MacBook M2 machines and one Intel Mac; appears OS-agnostic but more frequent on Ventura 13.x on M-series.
Zero-trust agent currently does not set explicit route metric on macOS for utun interface when tunnel is brought up after network interface changes (sleep/wake + captive portal flow).
Captive portal changes base interface properties (RA + new prefix) after tunnel establishment; timing causes the kernel to prefer the newly advertised prefix/interface.

Checked server-side: no change in peer keys or session — traffic is arriving at edge but source IPs show external interface, so responses are dropped by internal firewall rules expecting tunnel-sourced addresses.
Packet captures show TCP SYNs leaving via en7 and not being NATed through the tunnel gateway; returning packets never reach utun.
Related tickets: INT-302999 (similar post-sleep multihoming behavior) — differs because that one was primarily DHCP/MTU related, while this is IPv6 RA metric ordering + captive portal timing.
comments: Ava Martinez (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Logged after two engineers in SF reported inability to reach internal git and vault after waking laptops. Workaround was unplug/replug dock.
Jamal Singh (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced in lab with TS4 and Ventura VM. Captive portal RA arrives ~1-2s after utun up; kernel prefers en7 route. Collecting netstat/route and tcpdump.

SRE Team (#infra-help) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed that internal firewall blocks non-tunnel source IPs. Suggested forcing higher metric on physical interfaces or programmatically re-asserting tunnel route on sleep/resume.
Security - 2026-03-11: Need to avoid creating a fallback that leaks internal traffic to external networks. Any fix must preserve no-split-tunnel policy.
Jamal Singh - 2026-03-12: Drafted short-term agent patch to run a route preference adjustment on macOS when utun comes up. Testing patch v1.8.3-pre1 internally.
resolution: Workaround deployed: zero-trust-agent v1.8.3-pre1 (canary) now forces a higher-priority route for the utun interface on macOS immediately after tunnel establishment and re-applies after sleep/resume. For affected users we pushed the canary to the SF office and instructed to report if issue persists. Long-term: engineering will add deterministic route metric management and explicit IPv6 route rules in upcoming v1.9.0; also evaluating changing captive portal RA behavior with networking team to avoid late RA after auth. Follow-up: create a user script to run on login/sleep hooks for older devices and add test case to our CI that simulates RA arrival after tunnel establishment.
